posts.title: Complete Umrah Packing Checklist for Pakistani Pilgrims (2026)
posts.seoTitle: Umrah Packing Checklist 2026 — For Pakistani Pilgrims
posts.seoDescription: A practical, research-based Umrah packing checklist for Pakistani pilgrims — Ihram, documents, medicine, electronics, Makkah & Madinah essentials.
posts.author: Haiwad Ahmad
posts.authorBio: Haiwad Ahmad is Regional Branch Manager at Al Bari Travel & Tours, coordinating Umrah and Hajj groups out of Pakistan since 2018. He has personally accompanied over 40 group departures.
posts.excerpt: Most first-time pilgrims pack like it's a holiday — and then struggle in Makkah's 42°C heat with the wrong fabrics, missing documents, and bags too heavy for the buses. This checklist is built from what our group leaders actually carry, what airlines now allow, and what the Haramain authorities ask you to leave at home.
posts.body:
Packing for Umrah isn't like packing for a beach holiday. The weather changes between Makkah and Madinah, your luggage has to fit Saudia's strict weight limits, and once you're in Ihram a forgotten item can become a fidya (penalty) issue. This guide is the same checklist we hand to our own departing groups — refined over hundreds of pilgrims.

Documents (carry-on, never checked)

If you only get one section right, make it this one. A lost document at Jeddah immigration can cost you a full day.

  • Original Machine-Readable Passport (MRP) or e-Passport — valid for at least 6 months beyond return.
  • Printed Saudi e-Visa (A4) — even though it's electronic, immigration officers prefer a paper copy.
  • Yellow vaccination card showing meningococcal ACWY (mandatory) and current polio booster (mandatory for Pakistani nationals, valid 28 days–12 months).
  • Hotel vouchers for both Makkah and Madinah.
  • Air ticket printouts (e-ticket on your phone is allowed but officers still ask for paper).
  • 2 passport-size photos (white background, 4×6 cm).
  • Photocopies of all of the above kept in a different bag.
Tip from our group leaders: Email scanned copies of every document to yourself before you leave. If your luggage is delayed, you can still print at the hotel.

Ihram and clothing

Men's Ihram is two unstitched white cloths; women wear modest stitched clothing. Most pilgrims under-pack here and end up handwashing daily.

  • Men: 2 sets of Ihram cloth (one to wear, one spare), Ihram belt with zipped pocket, plastic Ihram slippers (no stitching across the top), pin-free fasteners.
  • Women: 3–4 loose abayas in breathable cotton, prayer scarves, comfortable walking shoes (not flip-flops — Masjid al-Haram floors get scorching).
  • Casual loose cotton or linen for after Umrah — Makkah averages 38–42°C April through October.
  • One warm layer for Madinah evenings (December–February dips to 8°C).
  • Socks for prayer halls (the floor is cold from air-conditioning).

Toiletries — and what NOT to bring

In Ihram, perfumed soap and scented products are forbidden for both men and women. Always pack unscented versions for the Ihram period, scented for after.

  • Unscented soap and unscented toothpaste (Sensodyne Original, Colgate Total Original).
  • Unscented shampoo (sachet form to save weight).
  • Toothbrush, miswak, dental floss.
  • Nail clippers (you cannot cut nails in Ihram — pack for before and after).
  • Vaseline (lips and feet crack from walking 5–10 km per day in dry air).
  • Wet wipes — non-alcoholic, unscented.
  • Universal travel adapter (Saudi uses Type G — UK 3-pin).

Medicine kit

Pharmacies are everywhere in Makkah and Madinah, but staff often don't speak Urdu and brand names differ. Bring a small labeled kit:

  • Panadol / Paracetamol — pilgrims walk far more than they expect.
  • Strepsils or similar — sore throat is the #1 complaint, caused by dust + AC.
  • Anti-diarrhoea (Imodium) and oral rehydration sachets (ORS).
  • Plasters for blisters, antiseptic cream, blister patches (Compeed-style).
  • Personal prescription medicines — bring the original doctor's note, in original packaging.
  • N95 or surgical masks — especially useful in tawaf crowds and during seasonal flu.
  • Sun-block SPF 50+ (allowed during Ihram only if odorless).

Electronics

  • Mobile phone — buy a Mobily, STC, or Zain SIM at Jeddah airport (around SAR 70–120 with data, ID required).
  • Power bank (10,000 mAh is the carry-on limit) — Masjid al-Haram floors have no convenient outlets.
  • Charger and cable for every device.
  • Small zip-pouch waterproof bag for phone — useful for ZamZam splashes during Tawaf.

Money and payment

Saudi accepts USD widely at exchange counters but you'll get the best rates inside Makkah at Al-Rajhi exchange branches. Carry a mix:

  • SAR 1,500–2,500 cash per person for a 14-day Umrah is a sensible buffer.
  • One debit card that works on Mada / Visa / Mastercard — confirm international withdrawal with your Pakistani bank before flying.
  • One backup card stored separately.
  • Small SAR notes (5, 10, 20) for tips and street food — large notes are hard to break.

What NOT to bring

Saudi customs is strict. The following will be confiscated and may delay you 2+ hours:

  • Alcohol of any kind (including mouthwash containing alcohol — pack Listerine Zero or non-alcoholic).
  • Pork products or anything containing pork derivatives.
  • Drones and powerful walkie-talkies.
  • Religious books or items considered idolatrous.
  • Strong vapes / e-cigarettes in large quantities — personal-use only.
  • More than 60,000 SAR equivalent in undeclared cash.

Luggage rules — Saudia, PIA, Air Sial, Emirates

Most carriers serving Pakistan–Jeddah/Madinah allow 30 kg checked + 7 kg cabin in Economy. Saudia and PIA also offer a free ZamZam allowance (5L on Saudia, 5L on PIA) collected at Jeddah airport — do not pack ZamZam yourself.

Final pre-departure routine

  1. Cut nails, trim hair, shower the night before (Sunnah for Ihram preparation).
  2. Apply non-perfumed deodorant only after entering Ihram.
  3. Check Umrah visa expiry — Saudi Umrah e-Visas are now usually 90-day single-entry.
  4. Take a printout of your hotel address in Arabic — useful for taxis.
  5. Download Nusuk app, Tawakkalna app, and Google Maps offline maps of both Makkah and Madinah.

faqs.q: Can I take ZamZam water in my checked luggage from Saudi Arabia?
faqs.a: No. Saudi customs and most airlines forbid passenger-packed ZamZam in checked or carry-on bags. Saudia, PIA, and Air Sial provide a free sealed 5-litre ZamZam allowance collected at Jeddah Airport's dedicated ZamZam counter after immigration.

faqs.q: How much luggage am I allowed on Umrah flights from Pakistan?
faqs.a: Economy class on Saudia, PIA, Air Sial, and Emirates from Pakistan to KSA generally allows 30 kg checked + 7 kg cabin. Business class is typically 40 kg. Always confirm with your airline at booking — Umrah season weight allowances sometimes vary.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring my own Ihram, or can I buy it in Saudi Arabia?
faqs.a: You can buy Ihram in any souq in Makkah and Madinah for SAR 30–80, but most pilgrims prefer to bring at least one set from Pakistan to wear at the Miqat. Many Pakistani airports (Lahore, Islamabad, Karachi) also have Ihram shops in the international departure lounge.

faqs.q: Are Pakistani polio boosters mandatory for Umrah?
faqs.a: Yes. Saudi authorities require all travellers from Pakistan to show proof of polio vaccination administered 4 weeks to 12 months before arrival. The booster is free at any government EPI centre in Pakistan. Bring the original yellow card to immigration.

faqs.q: Can women travel for Umrah without a Mahram?
faqs.a: As of 2022, Saudi Arabia permits women of any age to travel for Umrah without a Mahram. However, many pilgrims still travel in family groups or organised parties — both for comfort and to handle paperwork together.

faqs.q: What's the best small bag to use inside Masjid al-Haram?
faqs.a: A small zipped sling pouch or chest bag is ideal for phone, ID, cash, and prayer beads. Large backpacks are sometimes refused at certain Haram gates during peak times. Avoid loose pockets — Tawaf crowds make pickpocketing easy.

posts.title: First-Time Umrah Guide: 12 Things Every Pakistani Pilgrim Should Know
posts.seoTitle: First-Time Umrah Guide for Pakistani Pilgrims (2026)
posts.seoDescription: Everything a first-time Pakistani Umrah pilgrim needs to know — visa, Ihram, Miqat, Tawaf, Sa'i, halq, Madinah ziyarah, and the costly mistakes to avoid.
posts.author: Haiwad Ahmad
posts.excerpt: First-time pilgrims tell us the same things every season: 'I wish I had known about the Miqat before the plane started descending.' 'I didn't realise you cannot use scented soap.' 'I had no idea Sa'i was that long.' Here's a tight, plain-language guide built from those conversations — 12 things to know before you fly.
posts.body:
Umrah is one of the most personally moving experiences in a Muslim's life — but it is also a logistically detailed journey, and small mistakes (entering Ihram late, breaking Ihram rules, missing a rakat at the Multazam) can cost time, money, or a fidya. This guide assumes you've never done Umrah before. It walks through 12 things our first-time pilgrims wish they had known.

1. The Miqat is a hard boundary, not a suggestion

Anyone intending Umrah must enter the state of Ihram at or before the Miqat. For Pakistani pilgrims flying into Jeddah, the captain will normally announce when the plane crosses the Miqat boundary of Qarn al-Manazil (around 45 minutes before landing). For those flying into Madinah first, the Miqat is Dhu'l-Hulayfah (Bir Ali), a station you'll visit by bus from the Prophet's Mosque before continuing to Makkah.

2. Make your Niyyah and Talbiyah audibly

After putting on Ihram, declare your intention: Labbayk Allahumma Umratan, then begin the Talbiyah: Labbayk Allahumma labbayk… Recite it loudly (men) or quietly (women) and continue intermittently until you reach the Black Stone at the Kaabah.

3. Ihram restrictions are stricter than most people realise

While in Ihram you cannot:

  • Cut nails or hair
  • Apply perfume or scented products
  • Cover the head (men) or face (women) — though women may shield the face from male strangers without it touching the skin
  • Hunt or kill animals (mosquitoes excepted)
  • Marry, propose, or have intimate relations
  • Wear stitched clothing (men only)

Accidental violations require a fidya — usually a sheep or 6 fasts or 6 sadaqahs to the poor of Makkah. Deliberate violations are more serious. When in doubt, ask your group leader or a local scholar.

4. Tawaf is 7 laps — but harder than you think

One full circuit of the Kaabah is about 110–130 metres. Seven laps means roughly 1 km, but during peak hours (Asr–Maghrib, Friday night) the crowd doubles your time. Wear comfortable Ihram slippers, take a small water bottle, and start each lap by raising your right hand toward the Black Stone with Bismillah Allahu Akbar.

5. Sa'i is 3.5 km — pace yourself

Between Safa and Marwah is 450 metres. Seven trips (Safa → Marwah counts as one) totals about 3.5 km. Many first-timers walk straight from Tawaf into Sa'i and exhaust themselves. Drink water, use the wheelchair tracks if needed (rentable for SAR 100–200), and remember that running between the two green markers is for men only.

6. Halq vs Taqsir — choose carefully

To exit Ihram, men shave their heads (Halq, preferred) or trim a fingertip's length from all sides (Taqsir). Women trim only a fingertip's length of hair — they do not shave. Halq stations are everywhere outside Masjid al-Haram, charging SAR 10–20. Insist on a clean blade and a fresh razor.

7. ZamZam is everywhere and free

Don't carry water into the Haram — ZamZam dispensers and pre-filled cups line every level. The water from the original well is now distributed citywide via dedicated ZamZam taps in every mosque. Many pilgrims drink it standing, facing the Qiblah, in three breaths (Sunnah).

8. Prayer halls are gender-segregated and crowded

Men and women pray in separate sections. During peak Umrah season (Ramadan, summer school holidays), the Haram can hold 2.5 million people. Arrive 90 minutes before Maghrib to get a spot near the Kaabah. The third and fourth floor (and the rooftop) are far less crowded — and the view of the Kaabah is unmatched.

9. Madinah ziyarah is part of the journey — not the destination

Madinah is not part of Umrah, but almost every Pakistani group visits for 3–5 days before or after Makkah. The 8 rakat in Masjid al-Nabawi carry 1,000x reward; one prayer in Riyadul Jannah (the green-carpet area between the Prophet's grave and the original Minbar) carries immense significance. Riyadul Jannah now requires a free Nusuk app reservation — book it before you fly.

10. Saudi authorities use the Nusuk app for everything

Download Nusuk before you leave Pakistan. It handles:

  • Riyadul Jannah reservations
  • Rawda visit time slots
  • Tawaf permits in peak season (occasionally enforced)
  • Roshn Saudi pilgrim updates

You'll also use Tawakkalna for health declarations and Absher if you stay long enough to need any extension.

11. Beware Umrah scams

In both Makkah and Madinah you'll be offered:

  • 'Special tour' to caves, mountains, battlefield sites — most are pure tourism, often misrepresented as religious sites
  • 'Cheap' currency exchange in side streets — almost always counterfeit notes
  • 'Free' ZamZam delivery to hotel for high prices
  • 'VIP' Riyadul Jannah access — this is impossible to buy; only the free Nusuk app slots are valid

12. Plan for the journey home

Jeddah and Madinah airports get extremely crowded on Umrah-season departures. Arrive 4 hours early. Collect your free ZamZam at the dedicated counter after immigration. Carry a printed return ticket. Most importantly, perform Tawaf al-Wada (the Farewell Tawaf) before leaving Makkah — it is wajib for departing pilgrims.

faqs.q: How long does Umrah take to perform?
faqs.a: The Umrah rites themselves (Ihram → Tawaf → Sa'i → Halq) take 3–5 hours for an average pilgrim. The full Umrah journey from Pakistan is typically 10–14 nights, split between Makkah (7–10) and Madinah (3–5).

faqs.q: What is the minimum age to perform Umrah?
faqs.a: There is no minimum age — infants can be brought along. However, Saudi authorities require children's vaccination records, and many groups recommend waiting until a child is at least 7–10 so they remember the experience.

faqs.q: Do I need to memorise any specific duas for Umrah?
faqs.a: The only mandatory utterance is the Niyyah and Talbiyah. The duas during Tawaf, Sa'i, drinking ZamZam, and at Multazam are recommended but you can recite any sincere supplication in any language. Most Pakistani Umrah agencies provide a small pocket dua book.

faqs.q: Is Umrah obligatory in Islam?
faqs.a: Scholars differ. The majority of Hanafi scholars consider Umrah a strong Sunnah, while many Shafi'i and Hanbali scholars hold it as a one-time obligation for those who can afford it. Either way, it carries immense reward.

faqs.q: Can I perform Umrah more than once in a single trip?
faqs.a: Yes. Many pilgrims perform a second Umrah on behalf of a deceased parent or relative. To do so, exit the Haram, travel to a Miqat point (most pilgrims use Masjid Aisha at Tan'eem, just outside Makkah), enter Ihram again, and return to perform Tawaf and Sa'i.

posts.title: Saudi e-Visa for Umrah from Pakistan: Complete 2026 Guide
posts.seoTitle: Saudi e-Visa for Umrah from Pakistan 2026 — Step by Step
posts.seoDescription: How to apply for the Saudi Umrah e-Visa from Pakistan in 2026 — fees, processing time, documents, Nusuk Masar, and the difference vs traditional visa.
posts.author: Haiwad Ahmad
posts.excerpt: Saudi Arabia has overhauled its Umrah visa system since 2022. Pakistani pilgrims now have three valid routes — the traditional MoFA Umrah visa via a licensed Pakistani agent, the Nusuk Masar e-Visa for self-service applicants, and the Saudi tourist e-Visa (which also permits Umrah). Here's which route is right for whom, and how to apply correctly.
posts.body:
The Saudi visa landscape has changed more in the last 36 months than in the previous 30 years. Pakistani Umrah pilgrims today have far more flexibility than a generation ago — but also more confusion about which visa to apply for, who can issue it, and how to avoid rejection. This guide walks through the three current routes, the documents required, fees as of 2026, and the most common mistakes.

Route 1 — Traditional MoFA Umrah Visa via a Pakistani agent

This remains the most common route for Pakistani pilgrims travelling in organised groups. Your licensed Pakistani Umrah operator submits your file to a Saudi Mu'allim (ground-handling office in Saudi), which submits to MoFA Saudi for visa issuance.

  • Who it suits: Group travellers, families with multiple members, first-timers preferring full-service.
  • Processing time: 5–14 working days.
  • Fee: Visa itself is no longer free as of 2022 — Saudi charges roughly SAR 300 per pilgrim (~PKR 22,000 at current rates), often bundled into the package price.
  • Single or multiple entry: Single entry, 90 days validity, 30-day stay.

Route 2 — Nusuk Masar e-Visa

Launched in late 2022 and gradually expanded since, the Nusuk Masar platform lets individual pilgrims apply directly online without going through a Pakistani agent. Pakistan was added to the eligibility list in 2023.

  • Who it suits: Experienced pilgrims, single travellers, people already arranging their own hotels and flights.
  • Processing time: 24–72 hours.
  • Fee: SAR 535 (~PKR 39,000) including the visa fee, Tawakkalna health permit, and basic insurance.
  • Validity: 90 days single entry, 30-day stay.
  • Apply at: nusuk.sa (the official Saudi platform).

Route 3 — Saudi Tourist e-Visa (also permits Umrah)

Since 2019 (relaunched and expanded post-Covid), the standard Saudi Tourist e-Visa permits the holder to perform Umrah during the visit. This is now the most flexible route — multi-entry, 1 year validity, 90-day stay per visit.

  • Who it suits: Pilgrims who want to combine Umrah with tourism (Riyadh, AlUla, the Red Sea coast), or who travel to Saudi frequently.
  • Processing time: 1–5 minutes (instant approval common).
  • Fee: USD 137 (~PKR 38,000) including insurance.
  • Apply at: visa.visitsaudi.com
  • Catch: Pakistan is currently NOT on the e-Visa eligibility list for individual self-application. Pakistani nationals must apply via a Saudi embassy or consulate in Islamabad/Karachi or use Nusuk Masar instead.

Documents required (all routes)

  • Original Machine-Readable Passport with at least 6 months validity from the date of entry
  • One recent passport-size photograph (white background, no glasses, no head covering for men)
  • Confirmed return air ticket
  • Confirmed Saudi hotel booking (Makkah, Madinah, or both)
  • Yellow vaccination card showing meningococcal ACWY and polio booster
  • Bank statement (last 3 months) — sometimes requested for tourist visa route
  • NIC copy (front and back)

Common rejection reasons

  1. Passport validity less than 6 months from date of intended entry.
  2. Photograph not meeting Saudi MoFA specs (wrong background, glasses, smiling, head turned).
  3. Previous overstay on a Saudi visit/Umrah visa (results in 3-year ban from any Saudi visa).
  4. Conflicting hotel and ticket dates (e.g. hotel from 5th but flight returning 3rd).
  5. Applying for Umrah visa during Hajj season (June 1 to mid-July) — Saudi suspends Umrah visa issuance to non-Hajj pilgrims during the Hajj window.

Hajj-season blackout

Every year, Saudi suspends Umrah visa issuance from approximately Shawwal 15 to Dhu al-Hijjah 15 (roughly mid-April to mid-July depending on the lunar calendar). During this window, only confirmed Hajj pilgrims may enter for religious purposes. Pakistani applicants planning Umrah in May or June should aim to enter and exit before Shawwal 15.

What changes between Hajj years

Saudi authorities periodically revise rules. For Hajj 1448H / 2027 onward, MoFA has signalled tighter biometric capture at Pakistani VFS centres and expanded use of the Nusuk app for ground services. We update this guide each Saudi fiscal year (March–April) to reflect changes.

Need help? Our team handles Pakistani Umrah visa files daily through both the traditional MoFA route and Nusuk Masar. If you've been rejected once or want a single point of contact, WhatsApp us at +92 315 9596161.

faqs.q: How much does a Saudi Umrah visa cost from Pakistan in 2026?
faqs.a: The visa fee itself is approximately SAR 300 (~PKR 22,000), but the total cost a pilgrim pays depends on the route. Nusuk Masar charges SAR 535 inclusive. A full Umrah package via a licensed Pakistani agent typically bundles visa + hotel + transport + flight, so the visa cost is not shown separately.

faqs.q: Can I apply for Saudi Umrah visa myself online?
faqs.a: Yes — Pakistani nationals can apply directly via Nusuk Masar (nusuk.sa). You'll need a confirmed hotel, return ticket, and vaccination card. Processing is typically 24–72 hours.

faqs.q: How long is the Saudi Umrah visa valid?
faqs.a: Saudi Umrah e-Visas are valid for 90 days from issuance, single entry, with a maximum 30-day stay inside Saudi Arabia.

faqs.q: Can children travel on a Saudi Umrah visa?
faqs.a: Yes. Children of all ages, including infants, can be added to a parent's application. Each child needs their own passport, photo, and vaccination card (where age-appropriate).

faqs.q: What happens if I overstay my Saudi Umrah visa?
faqs.a: Saudi imposes a 3-year ban from any Saudi visa for overstays, plus a SAR 25,000 fine and potential deportation. Always exit before the stamped expiry date. If you fall ill or face emergency, contact your Pakistani embassy in Riyadh or consulate in Jeddah immediately.

faqs.q: Is the Hajj-season Umrah visa blackout still in force?
faqs.a: Yes. Saudi MoFA suspends Umrah visa issuance from approximately Shawwal 15 to Dhu al-Hijjah 15 each year. Pakistani pilgrims planning May–June Umrah should target dates before Shawwal 15.

posts.title: Best Months for Umrah from Pakistan (Weather, Cost & Crowds)
posts.seoTitle: Best Months for Umrah from Pakistan — 2026 Calendar
posts.seoDescription: Month-by-month analysis of Umrah from Pakistan — weather in Makkah & Madinah, hotel and flight prices, crowd density, and the cheapest 4 weeks of the year.
posts.author: Haiwad Ahmad
posts.excerpt: When you go for Umrah determines almost everything — what you pay, how crowded the Haram is, and whether you'll be standing in Makkah's 44°C July sun or its perfect 22°C January evening. This guide breaks down every month of the year for Pakistani pilgrims.
posts.body:
The question we get most often from first-time pilgrims is: 'When is the best time to go for Umrah?' The honest answer is — it depends on what you're optimising for. Cost-sensitive families avoid Ramadan and school holidays. Spiritually motivated pilgrims plan for the last 10 nights of Ramadan despite the price. Older pilgrims avoid the summer heat. This guide gives you everything you need to choose.

The three factors that matter

  1. Weather — Makkah can hit 45°C from June to August. Madinah is a few degrees cooler year-round.
  2. Cost — Ramadan and Hajj-adjacent months are the most expensive. November and late January are the cheapest.
  3. Crowds — Ramadan, school summer holidays, and winter break drive massive crowd density.

Month-by-month breakdown

January — Coolest weather, manageable crowds

Makkah averages 18–25°C. Madinah dips to 8°C at night. Hotel prices moderate. Best for elderly pilgrims, families with very young children, and anyone with health conditions affected by heat. Avoid early January — Pakistani winter school break creates a spike.

February — Best overall month

Mild weather, low crowds, lowest hotel prices of the year. If you have flexibility, February is our agency's most-recommended month. Many of our group leaders go themselves in February.

March — Mild but rising

Weather is comfortable (20–28°C). Prices start to climb as Ramadan approaches. Last 10 days of March can already see Ramadan pricing if Ramadan falls in early April.

April — Ramadan factor

Ramadan 2027 begins around Feb 17, 2027. Ramadan 2028 begins around Feb 6, 2028. When Ramadan falls in any part of April, prices triple. Outside Ramadan, April is warm (26–35°C) and moderate-crowd.

May — Pre-Hajj rush

Weather warming to 30–38°C. Some Pakistani Hajj pilgrims start arriving for early Hajj-related travel. Umrah visa rules tighten as Hajj season approaches. Avoid late May unless your Umrah visa is already issued.

June — Umrah visa blackout begins

Saudi typically stops issuing Umrah visas mid-May to mid-July. Temperatures soar to 40–44°C in Makkah. Madinah is a few degrees cooler but still hot. Not recommended.

July — Hajj month

No Umrah visas issued. Makkah is closed to non-Hajj pilgrims. Temperatures peak at 45°C.

August — Post-Hajj reopening

Umrah visa issuance resumes mid-August. Weather still 40°C+. Hotel prices reset (now empty after Hajj). For heat-tolerant pilgrims this is one of the cheapest months — but most Pakistani pilgrims wait for cooler weather.

September — Cooling and cheap

Temperatures fall to 35–40°C. Hotel prices low. Good combination of cost and tolerable heat. Madinah is noticeably cooler.

October — Sweet spot for value seekers

Weather drops to 28–35°C. Crowds light. Prices low. October is our second-most-recommended month after February for cost-conscious pilgrims.

November — Cheapest month of the year

Weather perfect (22–30°C). Hotel rates at their absolute lowest. Almost no Pakistani group travel — most agents have small private parties. If your top priority is cost-per-day, November wins.

December — Winter break spike

First half is similar to November. Second half (Pakistani school winter break) sees a 40–60% price spike. Weather excellent (18–28°C).

Ramadan Umrah — the special case

One Umrah in Ramadan equals one Hajj in reward (per the hadith). For this reason, Ramadan Umrah is in extraordinary demand. Pakistani pilgrims should know:

  • Hotel prices in Makkah tripled to quadrupled vs non-Ramadan months. A 3-star room near the Haram during last 10 nights can hit SAR 4,000+ per night.
  • Pakistani group packages for Ramadan Umrah sell out 4–6 months in advance.
  • The reward is greatest in the last 10 nights — but the crowds peak then too. Iftar inside Masjid al-Haram is unforgettable but logistically intense.
  • If you cannot afford Ramadan Umrah, the first 10 nights are far cheaper than the last 10.

Pakistani-specific timing factors

  • Pakistani school terms — winter break (mid-Dec to early Jan) and summer break (June–July) drive Pakistani family bookings. Avoid these windows for cheap rates.
  • Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha — most Pakistani agents close their direct booking lines for 3–5 days around each Eid.
  • September school start — many Pakistani families finish summer Umrah in late August so children start school on time. Late August is therefore packed with Pakistani groups.

Our recommendation by pilgrim type

Pilgrim TypeBest Month
Elderly / heat-sensitiveJanuary or November
Maximum spiritual rewardLast 10 nights of Ramadan
Cost-sensitive familyNovember or February
First-time pilgrimFebruary or October
School-age childrenJuly school holidays (heat-tolerant only) or December break (expensive)

faqs.q: What is the cheapest month for Umrah from Pakistan?
faqs.a: November is consistently the cheapest month, followed closely by February. Hotel rates in Makkah can be 50–60% lower than peak Ramadan rates. Flights from Pakistan to Jeddah and Madinah also tend to be lowest in these months.

faqs.q: When does Saudi Arabia stop issuing Umrah visas?
faqs.a: Saudi typically halts Umrah visa issuance from approximately mid-Shawwal (mid-May in most years) to mid-Dhu al-Hijjah (mid-July). The exact dates shift each Hijri year. Umrah visas resume in late July or early August.

faqs.q: Is it safe to go for Umrah in summer (June–August)?
faqs.a: Saudi authorities and most Pakistani agents discourage summer Umrah for the elderly, those with heart conditions, and children under 7. Makkah hits 45°C, the Haram floor (despite shade) reflects heat, and dehydration is the #1 health risk. If you must travel in summer, schedule Tawaf and outdoor activities for after Maghrib.

faqs.q: Should I go for Umrah in Ramadan?
faqs.a: If you can afford it and physically handle long fasting plus high crowds, Ramadan Umrah is the most spiritually rewarding time of year — especially the last 10 nights. If cost or stamina is a concern, the rest of the year is also blessed; Umrah is virtuous in any month.

faqs.q: What's the weather like in Madinah vs Makkah?
faqs.a: Madinah is consistently 3–6°C cooler than Makkah year-round, and winter nights can drop to 6–8°C. Bring at least one warm layer if travelling November to February. Makkah, being at lower altitude and surrounded by mountains, traps heat more.

posts.title: Umrah Visa vs Saudi Tourist Visa: What Pakistani Pilgrims Need to Know
posts.seoTitle: Umrah Visa vs Saudi Tourist Visa from Pakistan (2026)
posts.seoDescription: Side-by-side comparison of the Saudi Umrah visa and Saudi Tourist e-Visa for Pakistani pilgrims — fees, validity, multi-entry rules, and which to choose.
posts.author: Haiwad Ahmad
posts.excerpt: Since 2019, Saudi Arabia has allowed Tourist e-Visa holders to perform Umrah. This created confusion among Pakistani pilgrims: should you apply for a traditional Umrah visa, or a Tourist e-Visa? Here's the side-by-side comparison.
posts.body:
The Saudi visa system used to be simple: Umrah pilgrims got an Umrah visa, business travellers got a business visa, and tourism didn't exist as a category. That changed in 2019 with the launch of the Saudi Tourist e-Visa, which not only opened the Kingdom to leisure travel but also explicitly permits the holder to perform Umrah. Pakistani pilgrims today have to choose between the two.

The short answer

If you're going purely for Umrah and want the cheapest, easiest path — use the Umrah visa (via your Pakistani agent or Nusuk Masar). If you want to combine Umrah with tourism, plan to return within 12 months, or have a complex itinerary — the Tourist e-Visa is more flexible.

Side-by-side comparison

FeatureUmrah VisaTourist e-Visa
Cost (Pakistan, 2026)~SAR 300 (PKR 22,000) bundled in package, or SAR 535 via Nusuk Masar~USD 137 (PKR 38,000) including insurance — but Pakistan is currently NOT on the self-apply list
Validity90 days from issuance365 days from issuance
Stay per entry30 days max90 days max
EntriesSingleMultiple
Can perform Umrah?YesYes
Can enter from Pakistan?YesYes (via embassy/consulate)
Can visit Riyadh, AlUla, Red Sea?No — Makkah, Madinah, Jeddah onlyYes — anywhere in KSA
Processing time5–14 days (traditional) or 24–72 hours (Nusuk)1–5 days via embassy
Hajj-season blackout?Yes (mid-May to mid-July)No (but you can't perform Hajj on Tourist visa)

Why Pakistani pilgrims usually choose Umrah visa

  • It's cheaper for a one-off pilgrimage
  • Pakistani agents handle every step including hotel and transport
  • Most pilgrims have no plan to visit Riyadh or the Red Sea — they fly Karachi/Lahore/Islamabad → Madinah or Jeddah, perform Umrah, and return
  • Group bookings are easier under a single agent file

When Tourist e-Visa makes more sense

  • You're a frequent business traveller to KSA who wants to combine Umrah with work trips
  • You're planning a once-in-a-lifetime trip that includes Umrah + AlUla + Diriyah (the Saudi tourism circuit)
  • You want flexibility to return for a second Umrah within 12 months without re-applying
  • You're a Pakistani expat living in the Gulf where the Tourist e-Visa is easier to obtain

Things both visas have in common

  • Both allow Umrah
  • Both require yellow vaccination card (meningococcal + polio for Pakistanis)
  • Both require 6-month passport validity
  • Both require confirmed return ticket
  • Neither permits Hajj — Hajj requires a separate Hajj visa, granted only via the Hajj quota system
  • Both prohibit overstay (3-year ban + SAR 25,000 fine)

One scenario where it matters: Family Umrah + Riyadh visit

A common Pakistani family scenario: parents want Umrah, but adult children working in Riyadh want to host them for a week. Under an Umrah visa, the pilgrim is technically restricted to Makkah/Madinah/Jeddah and is supposed to leave after 30 days — visiting Riyadh would be a visa violation. A Tourist e-Visa lets the family do both legally.

How Pakistan's Tourist e-Visa eligibility might change

Saudi has been steadily expanding the eligibility list. Pakistan is currently in a 'consulate-only' category — Pakistani nationals must apply via the Saudi embassy in Islamabad or consulate in Karachi rather than the self-apply portal. There has been credible reporting since late 2024 that Saudi will add Pakistan to the self-apply list within the next 18 months. We update this guide when that happens.

faqs.q: Can I perform Umrah on a Saudi Tourist e-Visa?
faqs.a: Yes. Since 2019, Tourist e-Visa holders are explicitly permitted to perform Umrah during their visit. You will still need to enter Ihram at the Miqat, perform Tawaf, Sa'i, and Halq/Taqsir as normal.

faqs.q: Can I perform Hajj on a Tourist e-Visa?
faqs.a: No. Hajj requires a separate Hajj visa, granted only via the Saudi Hajj quota system through each country's authorised Hajj agencies. Attempting Hajj on a Tourist or Umrah visa is a violation and results in penalties.

faqs.q: Which visa is faster — Umrah or Tourist?
faqs.a: Nusuk Masar Umrah visa is fastest (24–72 hours). The Tourist e-Visa applied through the Pakistani Saudi embassy takes 1–5 days. Traditional MoFA Umrah visas via a Pakistani agent take 5–14 days.

faqs.q: Does the Saudi Tourist e-Visa let me visit during Hajj season?
faqs.a: Yes, the Tourist visa is valid year-round. However, Makkah is closed to non-Hajj pilgrims during the Hajj week itself (8th to 13th Dhu al-Hijjah), and accommodation is essentially impossible to find. Visiting other parts of Saudi during Hajj week is fine.

faqs.q: Is there a youth or senior discount on either visa?
faqs.a: No. Saudi visa fees are flat for all ages. Children under 6 are sometimes processed at a reduced fee under family applications via Nusuk Masar — check at time of booking.

posts.title: Family Umrah Packages from Pakistan: What to Look for in 2026
posts.seoTitle: Family Umrah Packages from Pakistan 2026 — Guide & Costs
posts.seoDescription: How to choose a family Umrah package from Pakistan — what's included, hotel proximity, transport, child policies, and typical PKR pricing in 2026.
posts.author: Haiwad Ahmad
posts.excerpt: Booking Umrah for a family of 4 or 5 from Pakistan is a different calculation than a single pilgrim. Hotel rooms, transport, meal plans, child policies, and visa logistics all multiply. This guide explains what a real Pakistani family Umrah package should include — and the warning signs that a 'cheap' package is hiding extra costs.
posts.body:
Family Umrah is one of our most common bookings. A typical Pakistani family of 5 (two parents, three children) faces a fundamentally different planning challenge than a single pilgrim. Hotel room sharing, separate prayer-time logistics for women, child-friendly meals, wheelchair access for elders, and the logistics of moving everyone between Madinah and Makkah safely — all of it adds up. Here's what to look for.

What a complete family Umrah package includes

  • Visa — Saudi Umrah visa for every family member, including infants
  • Airfare — Round trip from Lahore / Islamabad / Karachi to Madinah and back from Jeddah (or vice versa)
  • Hotel in Madinah — 3–5 nights, ideally within 200–400m of Masjid al-Nabawi
  • Hotel in Makkah — 7–10 nights, ideally within 300–600m of Masjid al-Haram (Ajyad / Misfalah / Shisha areas)
  • Ground transport — Jeddah/Madinah airport → hotel; Madinah → Makkah (4–5 hour journey); Makkah → airport
  • Ziyarat tours — usually 1 in Madinah (Quba, Uhud, Qiblatain) and 1 in Makkah (Cave Hira, Cave Thawr, Arafat, Mina)
  • Meals — breakfast included is standard; full board is upgraded
  • Mu'allim ground services in Saudi
  • Group leader who travels with you from Pakistan
  • Pre-departure briefing in Urdu/Pashto/Punjabi

Typical 2026 PKR pricing for a family of 4

Per-person rates × 4 give you a useful benchmark. These are realistic ranges for non-Ramadan, non-Hajj-adjacent months:

Package TierPer PersonFamily of 4 Total
Economy (3-star, 500m+ from Haram)PKR 240,000 – 290,000PKR 960,000 – 1,160,000
Standard (4-star, 200–400m from Haram)PKR 320,000 – 390,000PKR 1,280,000 – 1,560,000
Premium (5-star, within 100–200m, view of Haram)PKR 480,000 – 700,000PKR 1,920,000 – 2,800,000

Ramadan and December packages can be 60–100% above these rates.

Child pricing and policies

  • Infants (0–2): Most airlines charge 10% of adult fare, no airline seat. Saudi visa is full price. Hotel sharing free.
  • Children (2–11): Airline charges 75% of adult fare, hotel shares parents' room without extra bed for ~PKR 30,000–50,000 discount, separate visa.
  • Adults (12+): Full price.

Hotel proximity — the single biggest comfort factor

For a family, hotel distance from the Haram matters more than star rating. A 5-star at 800m means walking 1.6 km round-trip for every prayer, in 35°C+ heat — children and elders won't manage. A 3-star at 200m means a 2-minute walk and the ability to return between prayers to rest.

The closest Pakistani-friendly hotels in Makkah are clustered in three zones:

  1. Ajyad — south of the Haram, 200–400m. Mostly 3–4 star, mid-range.
  2. Misfalah — south-west, 300–600m. Many 4-star options, slight uphill walk back.
  3. Abraj Al-Bait / Clock Tower complex — directly above the Haram. 5-star only. PKR 800,000+ per person for a week.

In Madinah, the best Pakistani-family hotels are in the Central Area (Markaziya), within 200–500m of Masjid al-Nabawi.

Warning signs of a 'cheap' package hiding costs

  • 'Visa included' without specifying type — sometimes refers to a tourist visa that won't permit Umrah easily
  • Hotel name not specified, only star rating — agents reserve the right to assign you a far hotel
  • 'Buffet meals' but only breakfast actually included — read the fine print
  • Transport 'in Saudi only' — meaning you arrange your own Pakistani airport transfer
  • 'Group of 35–50' — too large for comfortable bus transport, hotel check-in delays
  • No named Pakistani group leader — you'll be handed to a Saudi Mu'allim who may not speak Urdu

What to ask before paying the deposit

  1. Which hotel exactly? (Insist on the name, not just the star rating.)
  2. How many metres from the Haram?
  3. Which floor will my family be assigned? (Lower floors are louder; higher floors require working elevators during peak crowds.)
  4. Is the room a triple or quad? Or are we expected to take two rooms?
  5. Who is my Pakistani group leader?
  6. What happens if my flight is delayed and I miss the Saudi onward bus?
  7. What is the cancellation policy if a family member falls ill?

faqs.q: Can I bring infants on a family Umrah package?
faqs.a: Yes. Infants (under 2) need a passport, a Saudi visa (most agencies process this), and meningococcal vaccination if old enough (typically from 6 months). Airline infant fare is around 10% of adult, no separate seat. Most hotels share infant cot free of charge.

faqs.q: Is wheelchair access available throughout the Umrah journey?
faqs.a: Yes. Most modern Makkah and Madinah hotels are wheelchair accessible. Wheelchairs can be rented at the Haram entrances for SAR 100–200 (with a deposit), and dedicated paved tracks for wheelchair Tawaf are clearly marked. Sa'i can also be performed in wheelchair.

faqs.q: What's the minimum age for a child to perform Umrah?
faqs.a: There is no minimum age. Even infants can be 'made' to perform Umrah by their guardian — the parent declares Niyyah on their behalf and carries them through Tawaf and Sa'i. Most families wait until at least age 7 so the child remembers the experience and can understand the rites.

faqs.q: Do family rooms with 4 beds exist in Makkah hotels?
faqs.a: Yes, but they're limited. Most Pakistani-family-friendly hotels in Ajyad and Misfalah offer triple and quad rooms. Quad rooms book out 3+ months in advance for Ramadan, peak Eid, and December travel. Always reserve early.

faqs.q: What should children pack differently from adults for Umrah?
faqs.a: Comfortable walking shoes (Crocs are popular for kids), refillable water bottles, snacks they're familiar with for hotel rooms, basic medicines (paracetamol syrup, ORS, anti-fever), a small entertainment item for the flight, and unscented soap/toothpaste for the Ihram period (children old enough for Ihram).

posts.title: Umrah from Lahore in 2026: Flights, Packages, and Logistics
posts.seoTitle: Umrah from Lahore 2026 — Flights, Packages, Costs
posts.seoDescription: Practical 2026 guide to Umrah from Lahore — direct flights to Madinah and Jeddah, package pricing, Allama Iqbal Airport tips, and Pakistani agent recommendations.
posts.author: Haiwad Ahmad
posts.excerpt: Lahore is the busiest Umrah departure city in Pakistan after Karachi. Allama Iqbal International Airport (LHE) has direct flights to both Madinah (MED) and Jeddah (JED) operated by PIA, Saudia, Air Sial, and FlyJinnah. This guide covers your real options, what to expect at LHE, and how to choose between Madinah-first and Jeddah-first itineraries.
posts.body:
Lahore-based pilgrims have one of the best Umrah connectivity options in the country. Five airlines operate direct flights from Allama Iqbal International Airport to Saudi Arabia, and the airport itself has dedicated Umrah pilgrim infrastructure including a Hajj/Umrah terminal lounge and Ihram changing facilities. Here's a practical 2026 guide.

Direct flights from Lahore (LHE)

To Madinah (MED)

  • PIA (PK): 4–5 weekly flights, ~5 hour journey, typically PKR 145,000–180,000 round trip in non-peak months
  • Saudia (SV): Daily flights, ~4.5 hour journey, slightly higher fare
  • Air Sial (PF): 3–4 weekly flights, often the cheapest option (PKR 130,000–165,000)

To Jeddah (JED)

  • PIA (PK): Daily flights
  • Saudia (SV): Daily flights
  • Air Sial (PF): 4–5 weekly
  • FlyJinnah (9P): 2–3 weekly, often cheapest budget option

Madinah-first vs Jeddah-first — which is better?

The Pakistani tradition is to fly into Madinah first, spend 3–5 days at Masjid al-Nabawi, then drive 4.5 hours to Makkah for Umrah. The pilgrim enters Ihram at the Miqat of Dhu'l-Hulayfah (Bir Ali) just outside Madinah.

Advantages of Madinah-first:

  • Easier on the body — start with cooler, calmer Madinah, build up to intense Makkah
  • Pakistani groups often start with collective Asr at Masjid al-Nabawi to set the mood
  • You enter Ihram at a proper Miqat station rather than mid-flight

Advantages of Jeddah-first (Makkah then Madinah):

  • You begin in the state of Ihram and complete Umrah within hours of landing — spiritually intense
  • You can then unwind in Madinah after the demanding rites
  • Flights to Jeddah are slightly cheaper

Most Pakistani Umrah packages from Lahore default to Madinah-first. Discuss the option with your agent based on what suits your family.

Lahore Airport (LHE) tips for Umrah travellers

  • Allama Iqbal International has a dedicated Hajj/Umrah pilgrim lounge in the international departure area — confirm with airline if you have access
  • Ihram changing rooms are available at the airport; many pilgrims change into Ihram here before security
  • Baggage allowance on Lahore–Saudi flights is 30 kg Economy + 7 kg cabin (Saudia, PIA, Air Sial all match)
  • Customs at Lahore rarely flags Umrah pilgrim luggage but will check for forbidden items on return (e.g. ZamZam in personal bags — illegal; use the airline's free 5L allowance instead)
  • Currency exchange at LHE is significantly more expensive than the market rate — exchange in Anarkali or DHA before going to the airport

Typical Lahore Umrah package pricing for 2026

TierIncludesPer Person PKR
Economy 14-day3-star hotels (500m+ from Haram), full visa, return ticket240,000 – 290,000
Standard 14-day4-star hotels (200–400m from Haram), full visa, return ticket, ziyarat tours340,000 – 410,000
Premium 14-day5-star hotels (within 100–200m), full visa, return ticket, ziyarat tours, full board meals520,000 – 750,000

Pre-departure checklist specific to Lahore pilgrims

  1. Visit any government EPI centre for the mandatory polio booster (free, valid 28 days to 12 months before travel)
  2. Get meningococcal ACWY vaccination at a private hospital (PKR 4,000–6,000 at Doctors Hospital, Hameed Latif, Aga Khan)
  3. Verify your passport has at least 6 months validity from departure date — renew at NADRA Mall Road if needed
  4. If using a private agent, confirm they are MoRA-licensed (verify on the Ministry of Religious Affairs website)
  5. For currency, withdraw PKR for petty cash but exchange to SAR at a reputable dealer (Pace Mall, Mall Road Anarkali) — never at the airport

Driving to Lahore from other Punjab cities

Many of our pilgrims drive in from Faisalabad, Multan, Sialkot, Gujranwala, and Sahiwal. Allama Iqbal Airport has paid parking (PKR 300/day in the long-stay lot), and the Motorway M2 makes the journey from anywhere in Punjab manageable. We recommend arriving 4 hours before international departure during Umrah season.

faqs.q: Which airline is cheapest for Umrah from Lahore?
faqs.a: Air Sial and FlyJinnah are typically the cheapest, often PKR 15,000–30,000 below PIA and Saudia for the same route. They serve Jeddah more reliably than Madinah. PIA and Saudia tend to be 10–20% more expensive but include more generous baggage and better connections in case of disruption.

faqs.q: How long is the drive from Madinah to Makkah?
faqs.a: Approximately 420 km, 4.5–5 hours by bus. Most Pakistani Umrah packages organise a daytime departure with a meal stop at Bir Ali Miqat or Badr. Some packages now use the Haramain High-Speed Rail (2 hours, around SAR 250 one-way), though this is usually an extra-cost upgrade.

faqs.q: Is there an airport in Makkah?
faqs.a: No. The nearest international airport to Makkah is Jeddah (JED), approximately 85 km away. From Jeddah Airport, ground transport to Makkah is around 1 hour by bus or car. Many Pakistani agents arrange direct hotel pick-up at Jeddah's dedicated Hajj/Umrah terminal.

faqs.q: Can I fly Lahore → Madinah → Makkah → Lahore on the same ticket?
faqs.a: Yes. The standard Pakistani Umrah itinerary is Lahore → Madinah, then driving to Makkah, then Jeddah → Lahore on return. Both PIA and Saudia book this 'multi-city' fare as a single ticket. Air Sial and FlyJinnah generally require two one-way bookings.

faqs.q: What's the best Umrah departure time of day from Lahore?
faqs.a: Late-night departures (post-midnight) from LHE are most common because they arrive in Saudi Arabia in the early morning, letting you check into your hotel by 10–11 AM Saudi time and rest before Maghrib. Daytime flights from LHE arrive in Saudi evening — you'll likely sleep first and start Umrah the next day.

posts.title: Umrah from Karachi in 2026: Flights, Costs, and What to Expect at JIAP
posts.seoTitle: Umrah from Karachi 2026 — Flights, Packages, Jinnah Airport
posts.seoDescription: Karachi Umrah guide for 2026 — direct flights to Madinah & Jeddah from JIAP, package pricing, Sindh agent options, and pre-departure logistics.
posts.author: Haiwad Ahmad
posts.excerpt: Karachi is Pakistan's largest Umrah departure hub. Jinnah International (KHI) offers the most frequent direct flights to Saudi Arabia of any Pakistani airport, with dedicated Hajj/Umrah pilgrim infrastructure. Here's what Karachi and Sindh pilgrims need to know in 2026.
posts.body:
Karachi has been a major Umrah departure city for over 70 years. Jinnah International Airport (JIAP / KHI) was the first Pakistani airport with dedicated Hajj terminal infrastructure, and today operates more weekly flights to Saudi Arabia than any other Pakistani city. This guide is for pilgrims based in Karachi and the wider Sindh region (Hyderabad, Sukkur, Mirpurkhas, Larkana).

Direct flights from Karachi (KHI)

To Madinah (MED)

  • PIA (PK): Daily flights, ~4.5 hour journey, PKR 145,000–185,000 round trip in non-peak months
  • Saudia (SV): Daily flights, slightly higher fare, generous baggage
  • Air Sial (PF): 3–4 weekly, cheapest option (PKR 125,000–160,000)
  • SereneAir (ER): 2 weekly flights, mid-tier

To Jeddah (JED)

  • PIA (PK): Daily flights, sometimes 2 per day in peak season
  • Saudia (SV): Daily flights
  • Air Sial (PF): 4–5 weekly
  • FlyJinnah (9P): 3–4 weekly, often the cheapest budget fare from KHI
  • Emirates / Etihad / Qatar via Dubai / Abu Dhabi / Doha: Convenient for longer Umrah + Gulf stopover trips, slightly higher fare

JIAP Hajj/Umrah Terminal — what to expect

Karachi has a dedicated Hajj/Umrah pilgrim terminal that operates during the Hajj and main Umrah seasons. It includes:

  • Separate check-in counters for Umrah pilgrims (reducing wait times)
  • Prayer halls and Wudu facilities
  • Ihram changing rooms
  • Briefing rooms used by Pakistani Mu'allim representatives
  • Free Pakistani breakfast service for some package pilgrims

Outside Hajj season, Umrah pilgrims use the standard international departure terminal. Allow 4 hours pre-departure during peak Umrah months.

Karachi Umrah package pricing (2026)

TierPer Person PKR
Economy 14-day (3-star, 500m+)235,000 – 285,000
Standard 14-day (4-star, 200–400m)335,000 – 405,000
Premium 14-day (5-star, within 200m)510,000 – 740,000

Karachi packages are typically PKR 5,000–10,000 cheaper than the equivalent Lahore package due to higher flight volume and competition. Ramadan and December packages can be 60–100% above these rates.

Pre-departure logistics specific to Karachi

  • Polio booster: Available free at any EPI centre. Major centres include Civil Hospital, Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre, and Sindh Government Hospital Liaquatabad.
  • Meningococcal vaccine: Available at Aga Khan University Hospital, Dr. Ziauddin Hospital, South City Hospital, and most private hospitals (PKR 4,000–6,500).
  • Yellow fever vaccination: Not required for Saudi Arabia from Pakistan, but if you've recently visited a yellow-fever country (sub-Saharan Africa, Brazil), you'll need proof.
  • Currency exchange: Mahmoodabad, Saddar, and Tariq Road have the most competitive SAR rates. Avoid airport exchanges.
  • Group leader meetings: Most reputable Karachi Umrah operators hold pre-departure briefings at their office or a community centre 2–3 days before flight.

What's different about Sindh-region pilgrims

Pakistanis from Hyderabad, Mirpurkhas, Larkana, and Sukkur often drive 2–6 hours to KHI. Tips:

  • Driving time from Hyderabad to KHI is 2.5–3 hours on the Karachi–Hyderabad Motorway (M9). Allow 5 hours minimum from arrival at airport to flight departure.
  • JIAP has paid parking; long-stay parking (Domestic side) costs PKR 300/day.
  • Coaches from Sukkur and Larkana to Karachi run overnight (Daewoo, Faisal Movers, Skyways) — match coach arrival to airport with at least 4-hour buffer.
  • Some agents in Hyderabad and Sukkur offer combined transport-to-Karachi-airport + Umrah package — saves logistics headache.

Common Karachi-specific mistakes

  1. Arriving at JIAP without confirming whether your Saudi visa was actually issued. (Some Pakistani agents quote 'visa included' but the file is processed only after deposit — confirm visa stamp 7 days before flight.)
  2. Choosing the absolute cheapest package without checking the hotel name and exact distance from Haram. A 'PKR 200,000 Umrah' is almost certainly a 800m+ hotel.
  3. Bringing ZamZam in personal luggage from Saudi — always use the airline's free 5L allowance at Jeddah/Madinah airport.
  4. Underestimating the Madinah → Makkah bus journey time. It's 5 hours including check-in, meal stop, and Miqat.

faqs.q: What's the cheapest airline for Umrah from Karachi?
faqs.a: Air Sial and FlyJinnah are typically PKR 20,000–35,000 below PIA and Saudia. They serve Jeddah more reliably than Madinah from Karachi. SereneAir's 2-weekly Madinah service is competitively priced when available.

faqs.q: How early should I arrive at Karachi Airport for an Umrah flight?
faqs.a: 4 hours minimum during Umrah peak season (Ramadan, July–August school holidays, December). 3 hours minimum off-season. The dedicated Hajj/Umrah terminal (when operational) processes pilgrims faster, but security and immigration queues can still be 60–90 minutes.

faqs.q: Can I fly Karachi → Madinah → Makkah → Karachi as one ticket?
faqs.a: Yes — PIA and Saudia book the standard multi-city Umrah itinerary (Karachi → Madinah, return from Jeddah → Karachi) as a single ticket. Air Sial and FlyJinnah generally require two separate one-way tickets, sometimes resulting in marginally higher overall cost.

faqs.q: Is there a direct flight from Karachi to Makkah?
faqs.a: No. There is no airport in Makkah. All pilgrims arrive at Jeddah (JED, 85 km from Makkah) or Madinah (MED, 420 km from Makkah). Ground transport is then organised by your Pakistani Umrah agent.

faqs.q: Do Karachi Umrah operators handle the visa themselves?
faqs.a: Reputable Karachi operators handle the Saudi MoFA Umrah visa file end-to-end as part of the package. They submit your documents to their Saudi Mu'allim, who submits to MoFA. The visa is electronically stamped on your passport copy. You should never need to visit a Saudi consulate yourself for an Umrah visa via this route.

posts.title: Hajj 2027 from Pakistan: Complete Step-by-Step Guide
posts.seoTitle: Hajj 2027 from Pakistan — Complete Guide & Application
posts.seoDescription: Everything Pakistani applicants need to know about Hajj 2027: government scheme vs private operators, costs, application timeline, documents, and quota.
posts.author: Haiwad Ahmad
posts.excerpt: Hajj 2027 (1448H) is expected to fall in late May to early June 2027. Pakistan's annual quota of approximately 179,210 pilgrims is split between the Government Hajj Scheme (administered by the Ministry of Religious Affairs) and Private Hajj Group Operators (HGOs). This guide walks through every step.
posts.body:
Hajj is the fifth pillar of Islam and the most logistically complex journey a Pakistani family will plan. Unlike Umrah (which can be performed in any month with a valid Saudi visa), Hajj is restricted to specific days of Dhu al-Hijjah, requires a dedicated Saudi Hajj visa, and is gated by national quotas. This guide explains the 2027 process from first decision to final farewell Tawaf.

When is Hajj 2027?

Hajj is performed from 8 to 13 Dhu al-Hijjah every Hijri year. For 1448H (2027 CE), this is approximately:

  • Yawm at-Tarwiyah (8 Dhu al-Hijjah): 26 May 2027 (approximate — confirmed by moon-sighting)
  • Yawm Arafah (9 Dhu al-Hijjah): 27 May 2027
  • Eid al-Adha (10 Dhu al-Hijjah): 28 May 2027
  • Days of Tashreeq (11–13 Dhu al-Hijjah): 29–31 May 2027

Pilgrim flights from Pakistan typically depart from mid-April to mid-May 2027 and return mid-June to mid-July 2027. Each pilgrim spends 35–45 days in Saudi Arabia depending on the package.

Pakistan's Hajj quota for 2027

Pakistan's quota is set annually by Saudi Arabia based on a 1-per-1,000-Muslims formula. Pakistan's quota for 2026 was 179,210; the 2027 quota is expected to be similar. This is split:

  • 50% Government Hajj Scheme via the Ministry of Religious Affairs and Inter-faith Harmony
  • 50% Private Hajj Group Operators (HGOs) — over 800 MoRA-licensed Pakistani operators

Step 1 — Decide: Government Scheme or Private?

See our dedicated comparison post for full detail. In short:

  • Government Scheme: Cheaper (PKR 1,075,000 – 1,175,000 for 2026), but lottery-based, basic services, larger crowd batches
  • Private: More expensive (PKR 1,400,000 – 2,800,000+), confirmed seat, choice of operator, better hotel proximity, smaller group

Step 2 — Application Timeline for Hajj 2027

TimeframeWhat Happens
October 2026MoRA announces Hajj Policy 2027 (cost, dates, application window)
November 2026Government Scheme application window opens (usually 10–15 days)
December 2026Lottery (Qura) draw for Government Scheme; results published
December 2026 – February 2027Private operators continue accepting bookings until their quota fills
January – February 2027Successful applicants pay second installment; medical screening begins
February – April 2027Document collection, visa processing, group leader briefings
Mid-April – mid-May 2027Pakistani Hajj flights depart
Mid-June – mid-July 2027Pakistani Hajj flights return

Step 3 — Eligibility requirements

  • Pakistani citizen with valid CNIC and Machine-Readable Passport
  • Age 12+ for solo pilgrim; children under 12 must travel with a parent/Mahram
  • Medically fit (medical screening required)
  • Mandatory vaccinations: meningococcal ACWY (within 3 years), polio booster (within 12 months), seasonal flu (recommended)
  • For women under 45: A Mahram (father, brother, husband, son) is required for the Government Scheme — Private operators have more flexibility under recent rules

Step 4 — Documents required

  • Original CNIC and 6 photocopies
  • Original Machine-Readable Passport (6 months validity from departure)
  • 4 passport-size photographs (white background, 4×6 cm)
  • Bank challan for Hajj fee deposit
  • Medical fitness certificate from a government hospital
  • Mahram nikah-nama or birth certificate proving relationship (for women)
  • Polio vaccination yellow card
  • Meningococcal ACWY certificate

Step 5 — The Hajj Journey

The full Pakistani Hajj experience is approximately 35–45 days:

  1. Departure week: Fly Pakistan → Madinah; check into Madinah hotel for 8–10 days of ziyarah and rest
  2. Pre-Hajj week: Travel to Makkah; settle into Makkah accommodation; perform Umrah of Tamattu
  3. Days of Hajj (8–13 Dhu al-Hijjah):
    • 8 Dhu al-Hijjah: Enter Ihram, travel to Mina
    • 9 Dhu al-Hijjah: Travel to Arafah for the standing (Wuquf); leave for Muzdalifah after Maghrib
    • 10 Dhu al-Hijjah: Stone Jamarat al-Aqaba; sacrifice (qurbani); shave/trim; return to Makkah for Tawaf al-Ifadah
    • 11–13 Dhu al-Hijjah: Stay in Mina; stone all three Jamarat each day
  4. Post-Hajj week: Rest in Makkah; perform Tawaf al-Wada (Farewell Tawaf); travel to Jeddah
  5. Return: Fly Jeddah → Pakistan

Step 6 — During Hajj, what to expect

  • Mina tents: Pakistani pilgrims are typically assigned in clusters by operator. Tents are air-conditioned, partitioned by gender. Sleeping mats provided.
  • Arafah: The most spiritually intense day. From dawn to sunset on 9 Dhu al-Hijjah, pilgrims stand in the plain of Arafah making dua. This single day is the essence of Hajj.
  • Muzdalifah: Pilgrims sleep under the open sky on the night of 9–10 Dhu al-Hijjah. Collect 49–70 pebbles for the stoning ritual.
  • Jamarat: Three pillars representing the rejection of Satan. The new Jamarat Bridge handles millions safely but is still a crowded experience. Follow your group leader's instructions strictly.
  • Qurbani: Most Pakistani pilgrims now pay for the qurbani electronically via the Saudi Adahi system, eliminating the need to be physically present at the slaughterhouse.

What can go wrong — and how to prepare

  • Heat exhaustion: Saudi temperatures in late May/early June 2027 will be 38–43°C. Drink water constantly. Wear lightweight Ihram. Don't skip meals.
  • Getting lost: Memorise your tent number and your group leader's mobile. Have your Saudi SIM activated. Pakistani embassy in Riyadh and consulate in Jeddah maintain 24/7 Hajj helplines.
  • Lost passport: Report immediately to your group leader; Pakistani consulate issues emergency travel documents.
  • Illness during Hajj: Saudi Red Crescent operates clinics at every Hajj station. Pakistani Hajj Mission also maintains a dedicated medical mission with Urdu-speaking doctors.

faqs.q: How much does Hajj 2027 cost from Pakistan?
faqs.a: Government Hajj Scheme 2027 is expected to be PKR 1,150,000 – 1,300,000. Private Hajj operator packages range from PKR 1,500,000 (basic) to PKR 3,500,000+ (premium 5-star with Aziziya tents). Final pricing is announced via the MoRA Hajj Policy 2027 expected in October–November 2026.

faqs.q: When does Hajj 2027 application open in Pakistan?
faqs.a: The Government Hajj Scheme application window typically opens in November and runs for 10–15 days, followed by a lottery (Qura) in December. Private operators usually accept bookings from October 2026 through February 2027 (or until their quota fills, whichever is sooner).

faqs.q: What is the difference between Hajj and Umrah?
faqs.a: Hajj is the 5th pillar of Islam, obligatory once in a lifetime for Muslims who can afford it, and performed only on 8–13 Dhu al-Hijjah. Umrah is a voluntary (but highly recommended) lesser pilgrimage performed at any time of year. Hajj has additional rites (Arafah, Muzdalifah, Mina, stoning of Jamarat, qurbani) absent from Umrah.

faqs.q: Can women perform Hajj without a Mahram?
faqs.a: Saudi Arabia has permitted women aged 45+ to perform Hajj without a Mahram in supervised groups since 2021. For women under 45, the Mahram requirement is still typically enforced. Some private Pakistani operators have additional flexibility — check directly. The Government Scheme remains strict on this rule.

faqs.q: How long is the Pakistani Hajj package in Saudi Arabia?
faqs.a: Standard Pakistani Hajj packages are 35–45 days in Saudi. This covers Madinah ziyarah (8–10 days), Makkah pre-Hajj (5–7 days), the Hajj rites themselves (5–6 days), post-Hajj rest (3–5 days), and travel buffers. Short packages of 25–30 days exist but compress the Madinah portion significantly.

faqs.q: Is the Hajj quota guaranteed once I apply?
faqs.a: No. The Government Hajj Scheme is lottery-based — applying does not guarantee selection. Private operator quotas are first-come-first-served until their licensed allocation fills. Always confirm quota confirmation before paying a large deposit.

posts.title: Government Hajj Scheme vs Private Hajj Operators in Pakistan
posts.seoTitle: Government vs Private Hajj 2027 Pakistan — Compared
posts.seoDescription: Side-by-side comparison of the Pakistan Government Hajj Scheme and private Hajj operators — cost, services, lottery, hotel proximity, and which to choose.
posts.author: Haiwad Ahmad
posts.excerpt: Pakistan's Hajj quota of approximately 179,210 pilgrims is split 50/50 between the Government Hajj Scheme (cheaper, lottery-based, basic services) and Private Hajj Group Operators (more expensive, confirmed seat, varying levels of service). Here's a clear-eyed comparison to help you choose.
posts.body:
Choosing between the Pakistan Government Hajj Scheme and a private Hajj Group Operator (HGO) is one of the biggest decisions a Pakistani Hajj applicant will make. Both routes lead to the same Hajj rites, but the experience, cost, certainty of seat, and quality of service differ substantially. This guide breaks down the comparison fairly.

The basics

Saudi Arabia allocates Pakistan an annual Hajj quota (179,210 in 2026; similar expected for 2027). The Ministry of Religious Affairs and Inter-faith Harmony (MoRA) splits this:

  • ~50% to the Government Hajj Scheme (administered directly by MoRA)
  • ~50% to Private Hajj Group Operators (over 800 MoRA-licensed companies)

Cost comparison (2026 actuals, 2027 estimates)

ItemGovernment SchemePrivate (Basic)Private (Premium)
2026 actual costPKR 1,075,000 – 1,175,000PKR 1,400,000 – 1,800,000PKR 2,400,000 – 3,200,000+
2027 expectedPKR 1,150,000 – 1,300,000PKR 1,500,000 – 1,950,000PKR 2,600,000 – 3,500,000+

Cost-saving cushion: short Hajj packages

Some private operators offer shorter Hajj packages (22–25 days vs the standard 35–45 days), reducing hotel and meal costs. These can be 20–30% cheaper than standard private packages but compress your Madinah experience.

The Government Hajj Scheme

Pros

  • Cheapest available Hajj option
  • Operated by experienced MoRA staff with established Saudi infrastructure
  • Includes basic medical mission with Urdu-speaking doctors
  • Established Pakistani embassy/consulate support pipeline
  • Refund mechanism if not selected in lottery

Cons

  • Lottery-based — applying does not guarantee a seat. Over-subscription is typical (in 2024, over 510,000 applied for ~90,000 government seats)
  • Limited choice of hotel quality and proximity to Haram
  • Larger pilgrim batches (sometimes 80–100 per group leader)
  • Less flexibility on departure dates and airline preference
  • Mahram requirement strictly enforced for women under 45

Private Hajj Operators

Pros

  • Confirmed seat once you book (first-come-first-served until quota fills)
  • Choice of hotel star rating and distance from Haram
  • Smaller group sizes (20–40 per group leader is typical)
  • Choice of airline (PIA, Saudia, Air Sial, FlyJinnah)
  • Customised meal plans (Pakistani vs continental)
  • Better Mina tent locations (some premium operators secure Wadi Muhassir-area tents very close to Jamarat)
  • More personalised group-leader attention and pre-departure briefings

Cons

  • Significantly more expensive (30–200%+ over Government Scheme)
  • Quality varies enormously between operators — some are excellent, some are barely better than the Government Scheme at 2x the price
  • Risk of unscrupulous operators (always verify MoRA license)
  • Limited recourse if operator fails to deliver promised services (some pilgrims have arrived in Saudi to find their advertised 4-star is actually 800m from Haram in a poor building)

How to verify a private operator's MoRA license

Visit the Ministry of Religious Affairs Pakistan website (mora.gov.pk) and look for the published list of licensed Hajj Group Operators (HGOs). Each licensed operator has a unique license number. Cross-check this number against the operator's claim. Never pay a deposit to an operator who cannot show you their MoRA HGO license certificate.

What 'premium' Hajj packages actually mean

'Premium' is loosely used. Look for these specific markers:

  • 5-star Makkah hotel within 200m of Haram — Hilton Suites Makkah, Pullman ZamZam, Swissôtel, Movenpick
  • 5-star Madinah hotel within 200m of Masjid al-Nabawi — Dar Al Taqwa, Anwar Al Madinah Movenpick, Pullman Zamzam Madina
  • Mina tents in Wadi Muhassir zone — closest to Jamarat, less walking
  • Aziziya accommodation for the pre-Hajj/post-Hajj phase (not just packed hotels)
  • Group size ≤ 25 per group leader
  • Full board Pakistani meals throughout
  • Dedicated Pakistani group leader with at least 10 prior Hajj seasons

Our honest take

For first-time Hajj pilgrims with budget flexibility, a reputable mid-tier private operator (PKR 1,800,000 – 2,200,000) usually offers the best balance of cost, comfort, and certainty. The Government Scheme is excellent value for experienced pilgrims or those for whom budget is the primary constraint. Premium private (PKR 2,500,000+) is appropriate for elderly pilgrims, those with health conditions, or families who specifically value 5-star comfort.

Always read the package terms carefully, verify the MoRA license, and demand the exact hotel name and Mina tent zone in writing before paying.

faqs.q: Is the Pakistan Government Hajj Scheme cheaper than private operators?
faqs.a: Yes, significantly. The Government Scheme typically costs PKR 1,075,000–1,175,000 (2026) while private packages start around PKR 1,400,000 for basic and exceed PKR 3,000,000 for premium. The gap reflects different hotel quality, group sizes, meal plans, and proximity to the Haram.

faqs.q: Can I switch from Government Scheme to private if not selected in lottery?
faqs.a: Yes. Many Pakistani applicants apply to the Government Scheme first and switch to a private operator after the December lottery results. However, private quotas fill fast — don't wait until February to book privately if you're concerned about availability.

faqs.q: Is the Government Hajj Scheme refundable if I'm not selected?
faqs.a: Yes. If your name is not drawn in the lottery, the full Government Scheme deposit is refundable. Refund processing typically takes 4–8 weeks after results.

faqs.q: What happens if a private Hajj operator fails to deliver promised services?
faqs.a: Complaints can be filed with the Ministry of Religious Affairs (MoRA) Hajj Cell, which can suspend or revoke an operator's HGO license. In practice, recovery of advance fees can be difficult. The strongest protection is verifying the operator's MoRA license and reading the contract carefully before paying.

faqs.q: Do private Hajj operators arrange transport from my home city to Karachi/Lahore?
faqs.a: Many do, especially those with regional branches. Confirm at booking. Some operators charge separately for inter-city transport; others bundle it into the package price.

faqs.q: Is the Hajj Mahram requirement still in force in 2027?
faqs.a: The Government Scheme strictly enforces the Mahram requirement for women under 45. Saudi authorities have relaxed the requirement for women aged 45+ in supervised groups, and some private operators have additional flexibility. Always confirm with your specific operator and check the latest MoRA Hajj Policy when published.

posts.title: Hajj Day-by-Day Rituals: A Pakistani Pilgrim's Guide
posts.seoTitle: Hajj Day-by-Day Rituals Guide for Pakistani Pilgrims
posts.seoDescription: Day-by-day Hajj guide for Pakistani pilgrims — 8 to 13 Dhu al-Hijjah, with the rites of Mina, Arafah, Muzdalifah, Jamarat, qurbani, and Tawaf al-Ifadah.
posts.author: Haiwad Ahmad
posts.excerpt: The 5–6 days of actual Hajj rites (8 to 13 Dhu al-Hijjah) are physically and spiritually intense. This day-by-day guide walks Pakistani pilgrims through each station, what to expect at Mina, Arafah, Muzdalifah, and Jamarat, and the common mistakes to avoid.
posts.body:
The Hajj rites condense into just 5–6 days of the year — 8 to 13 Dhu al-Hijjah — but they include the most spiritually charged moments of any Muslim's life. This guide walks Pakistani pilgrims through each day, what your group leader should be doing, and the small mistakes that cause stress or fidya (penalty).

The night before — 7 Dhu al-Hijjah

You've already arrived in Makkah from Madinah days or weeks earlier. By now you've performed Umrah of Tamattu (if you're a Tamattu pilgrim — the most common type for Pakistanis). On the evening of 7 Dhu al-Hijjah, your group will brief you on the next day's schedule. Sleep early — you'll need the rest.

Day 1 — 8 Dhu al-Hijjah (Yawm at-Tarwiyah)

  1. After Fajr, perform Ghusl (full ritual bath) and put on Ihram (men: 2 white cloths; women: modest stitched clothing).
  2. Declare the Niyyah for Hajj: Labbayk Allahumma Hajjan
  3. Recite the Talbiyah loudly (men) or quietly (women): Labbayk Allahumma labbayk…
  4. Travel to Mina by bus (Pakistani groups depart in waves from 6 AM onwards). The 8 km journey can take 1–4 hours depending on traffic.
  5. Arrive at your assigned Pakistani tent in Mina. Identify the tent number and group leader's location.
  6. Spend the day in worship, dua, and Qur'an recitation. Pray Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha, and Fajr (of 9 Dhu al-Hijjah) shortened (qasr) but not combined.
  7. Avoid leaving the Pakistani tent area — getting lost in Mina without your group is a real risk.

Day 2 — 9 Dhu al-Hijjah (Yawm Arafah — The Day of Hajj)

This is THE day. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Al-Hajju Arafah' — Hajj IS Arafah. Standing on Arafah from Zawal (just after noon) to sunset is the essential pillar of Hajj. If you miss this, you have not performed Hajj.

  1. After Fajr in Mina, travel by bus to Arafah (15–20 km, typically 1–3 hours in heavy traffic). Some Pakistani groups now depart before Fajr to reach Arafah early.
  2. Settle in your Arafah tent. Pray Zuhr and Asr together in shortened form (jam' and qasr) at the time of Zuhr — this is a strong Sunnah.
  3. From Zawal to sunset, stand in continuous dua. This is the most rewarded dua of the year. Face the Qiblah. Be humble. Cry. Ask for everything — for yourself, your family, the Ummah.
  4. The Prophet ﷺ said the best dua is: La ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamd wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadeer.
  5. After sunset, do NOT pray Maghrib. Board your bus to Muzdalifah immediately.

Day 2 (continued) — Night of 9–10 Dhu al-Hijjah (Muzdalifah)

  1. Arrive at Muzdalifah (~10 km from Arafah, can take 2–5 hours of bus crawl).
  2. Pray Maghrib and Isha together (combined) on arrival.
  3. Sleep on the open ground. There are no tents in Muzdalifah — pilgrims sleep under the stars on prayer mats.
  4. Collect 49–70 pebbles (small stones, slightly larger than a chickpea) for the stoning ritual of the next days.
  5. Stay until at least after Fajr. Elderly, women, and weak pilgrims may leave after midnight per Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ.

Day 3 — 10 Dhu al-Hijjah (Yawm an-Nahr / Eid al-Adha)

The busiest single day of Hajj. Five separate rites all happen between dawn and night.

  1. Stone Jamarat al-Aqaba — the largest of the three pillars. Throw 7 pebbles, one at a time, reciting Bismillah Allahu Akbar with each.
  2. Qurbani (sacrifice) — most Pakistani pilgrims pay for the qurbani electronically via the Saudi Adahi system. Receipt is issued; you no longer need to be physically present at the slaughterhouse.
  3. Halq or Taqsir — men shave the head (preferred) or trim. Women trim a fingertip's length.
  4. Exit Ihram (Tahallul al-Awwal) — after Halq/Taqsir, you exit Ihram. Most restrictions are lifted EXCEPT intimate relations with spouse.
  5. Tawaf al-Ifadah — return to Makkah and perform 7 laps of Tawaf at the Kaabah, followed by 7 laps of Sa'i. After this, all Ihram restrictions are lifted (Tahallul ath-Thani).
  6. Return to Mina by Maghrib if possible.

Day 4 — 11 Dhu al-Hijjah (First Day of Tashreeq)

  1. Spend the day and night in Mina.
  2. After Zawal (just past noon), stone all three Jamarat in order: small (Jamarat al-Sughra), middle (Jamarat al-Wusta), large (Jamarat al-Kubra/Aqaba). 7 pebbles each, 21 total.
  3. Make dua at the small and middle Jamarat after stoning. No dua at the large Jamarat (Sunnah).
  4. Sleep in Mina.

Day 5 — 12 Dhu al-Hijjah (Second Day of Tashreeq)

  1. Same as Day 4: stone all three Jamarat after Zawal.
  2. Pilgrims who wish to leave Mina early (Ta'ajjul) may depart before Maghrib of 12 Dhu al-Hijjah — but you MUST leave before sunset, otherwise you must stay for Day 6.
  3. Pilgrims staying for Day 6 spend a third night in Mina.

Day 6 (optional) — 13 Dhu al-Hijjah (Third Day of Tashreeq)

  1. For pilgrims who stayed in Mina, stone all three Jamarat one final time after Zawal.
  2. Then return to Makkah.

Final Rite — Tawaf al-Wada (Farewell Tawaf)

Before leaving Makkah for Pakistan, every Hajj pilgrim must perform Tawaf al-Wada — 7 laps of Tawaf at the Kaabah. This is wajib (obligatory). Menstruating women are exempted.

Common mistakes Pakistani pilgrims make

  • Not realising shortened (qasr) prayer in Mina is for travellers — Saudi residents pray full
  • Missing the Arafah window by arriving after Zawal or leaving before sunset
  • Praying Maghrib in Arafah (forbidden — pray it combined with Isha in Muzdalifah)
  • Stoning before Zawal on the days of Tashreeq (invalid — must be after Zawal)
  • Departing Muzdalifah before midnight without a valid Sunnah excuse
  • Forgetting to perform Tawaf al-Ifadah before leaving Makkah — this is a pillar of Hajj
  • Stoning all 21 pebbles into one Jamarat instead of 7 each

faqs.q: What is the most important day of Hajj?
faqs.a: 9 Dhu al-Hijjah — the Day of Arafah. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Hajj is Arafah.' Standing in the plain of Arafah from Zawal to sunset on this day is the essential pillar without which Hajj is not valid.

faqs.q: Can I leave Muzdalifah early on the night of 9–10 Dhu al-Hijjah?
faqs.a: Yes, for the elderly, women, weak pilgrims, and those caring for them. The Prophet ﷺ permitted these groups to leave after midnight. For other pilgrims, staying until after Fajr is recommended.

faqs.q: How do I know how many pebbles to collect at Muzdalifah?
faqs.a: 49 pebbles minimum (7 on 10 Dhu al-Hijjah at Jamarat al-Aqaba + 21 each on 11 and 12 Dhu al-Hijjah). If staying for 13 Dhu al-Hijjah, collect 70. Most pilgrims collect 70 to be safe — extra pebbles are simply unused.

faqs.q: Is qurbani included in Pakistani Hajj packages?
faqs.a: Most reputable Pakistani Hajj packages include the qurbani fee. The pilgrim signs up via the Saudi Adahi (sacrifice voucher) system electronically, and a receipt is issued. Verify with your operator at booking that this is included — some basic packages exclude it.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the Tawaf al-Ifadah on 10 Dhu al-Hijjah?
faqs.a: You can perform Tawaf al-Ifadah any time before leaving Makkah. Many Pakistani pilgrims perform it on 11 or 12 Dhu al-Hijjah due to crowd congestion on 10 Dhu al-Hijjah. However, until you perform Tawaf al-Ifadah, intimate relations with spouse remain prohibited.

faqs.q: Can I perform Hajj without ever doing Sa'i if I already did it during my Umrah of Tamattu?
faqs.a: For Tamattu pilgrims (the most common Pakistani choice), Sa'i is performed twice — once with Umrah and once with Hajj (after Tawaf al-Ifadah). For Qiran pilgrims, one Sa'i suffices. For Ifrad pilgrims, the Sa'i during Tawaf al-Ifadah is sufficient. Confirm your Hajj type with your group leader.

posts.title: How Much Does Hajj from Pakistan Cost in 2027? Real Breakdown
posts.seoTitle: Hajj from Pakistan Cost 2027 — PKR Breakdown by Tier
posts.seoDescription: Real cost breakdown of Hajj from Pakistan in 2027 — government scheme vs private packages, what's included, hidden costs, and PKR pricing by tier.
posts.author: Haiwad Ahmad
posts.excerpt: Hajj from Pakistan in 2027 is expected to range from PKR 1,150,000 (basic Government Scheme) to PKR 3,500,000+ (premium private packages). This is a transparent breakdown of where the money actually goes, what's included, and what hidden costs to budget for.
posts.body:
Hajj is one of the largest single expenses a Pakistani family will undertake. Costs have risen significantly over the past decade due to Saudi infrastructure fees, currency devaluation, and rising hotel rates in Makkah. This guide gives you a realistic 2027 budget — what you'll actually pay, what's included, and what extras to expect.

2027 Hajj cost ranges (estimated)

TierPer Person PKRApproximate USD
Government Scheme1,150,000 – 1,300,000$4,100 – $4,650
Private Basic1,500,000 – 1,950,000$5,350 – $6,950
Private Standard2,000,000 – 2,500,000$7,150 – $8,950
Private Premium (5-star)2,600,000 – 3,500,000+$9,300 – $12,500+

Where the money actually goes (typical private standard package)

ComponentApprox % of CostApprox PKR
Saudi government fees (visa, Mu'allim, tents in Mina/Arafah)22%440,000
Round-trip airfare Pakistan ↔ Saudi14%280,000
Hotel in Makkah (15+ nights)30%600,000
Hotel in Madinah (8–10 nights)13%260,000
Meals (breakfast included; full board on premium)5%100,000
Ground transport (airport, Madinah↔Makkah, Mina shuttles)5%100,000
Ziyarat tours (Madinah and Makkah)2%40,000
Qurbani (sacrifice via Adahi voucher)3%60,000
Operator margin, insurance, briefings, group leader6%120,000

Why Hajj costs vary so widely

  • Hotel proximity to Haram: A room 100m from Masjid al-Haram costs 4–6x a room 800m away. This single factor accounts for most of the price gap.
